notes:
Scope this round: non-coachmark copy for DARKNET.LNK, the gridlock endReason, result-screen rows, the CLEAN RUN desc, two new MANUAL.TXT sections, and two small noun swaps (patch cell -> patch piece) in existing duel strings. This replaces this agent's prior proposal file (story-retune-1 cycle); that content has already integrated into the shipped game and is not being resubmitted. Per this round's explicit instruction, coachmark copy is deliberately excluded; pipeline/copy/orders/ currently has no open orders from the tutorial-agent (checked, none found), so no teach-copy items are included here. They will be fulfilled in the follow-up round once filed. Item type used for this round's deliverables is 'ui-copy' (not one of the schema's named types, since none of them fit bespoke UI/system-voice string rewrites); each carries an explicit 'target' pointing at the exact call site so the Orchestrator can drop the string in without hunting. Loremaster flag: DARKNET.LNK's dealer is written as a fully anonymous handle ('SELLER: SIGNAL SCRAMBLED, NO ID ON FILE'), never a proper name, consistent with the world's naming law and with how a real gray-market listing reads. Story-ledger note candidate for the Loremaster to weigh, not written into any lore file: a named, on-screen dealer is not needed, but there may be a future hook in the dealer's cash-only, no-questions anonymity mirroring Dad's own secrecy (weekly cash suppressants, no ticket, no client on the back-room tower) without touching ground truth; recommend staying anonymous unless a later arc wants to use the dealer as that mirror. Integration note, not a new item: several existing UI strings elsewhere ('BUY PATCH CELL', 'PATCH CELLS X/Y', the KitScreen pouch card paragraph in screens.tsx) still say 'patch cell' and were not in this round's item list; they likely get superseded outright by ux-agent's patch-pouch-strip and darknet-window ui-specs, but flagging for a consistency sweep so no stray 'cell' language survives the piece rename.

Round 2 addendum (same brief, copy-order fulfillment pass): the five open orders tutorial-agent filed against this cycle's teaching-moments (patch-cell-use, night-shop, patch-craft, augment-draft line 2, boost-swap) are filled in place at pipeline/copy/orders/ and mirrored below as 'teach-copy' items. Voice check against shipped content/teaching.ts: matched the existing coachmark register (short declaratives, implicit or explicit second person, one line for the action/cost, one for the rule that changes what the player does), not the story-scene voice from the items above. patch-cell-use keeps the shipped moment's tactical closer ('the wall you cannot route around') while swapping in the new no-rotation rule. night-shop prioritizes the lost-determinism fact first per the order's stated priority, then folds in the unchanged night-patch framing and the new boost-bay purchase in the same second line since both fit under 160 chars; nothing was cut. patch-craft states the union-and-legality rule from the MANUAL.TXT PATCH PIECES paragraph (already filed above) in coachmark form, adding the stakes (both pieces spend regardless of the legality check) the reference section does not need to carry. augment-draft-line2 keeps line 1 verbatim from shipped teaching.ts and rewrites only line 2: kept the CONFIG/BOOST clause and the three-tickets cadence per the order's instruction to preserve verified facts, added a closing clause naming the swap behavior (a full bay swaps instead of blocking) so the line does not read as though the pool could ever run dry, and did not restate any catalog count. boost-swap is new; led with the forced choice (bench one you own) before the CONFIG exemption, since the order named that ordering as the more important fact. No ledger conflicts: none of these five touch Rhea, Dad, or Patch, they are pure mechanic teaching, so the reveal-schedule table in lore/ledger.md does not apply.

items.notes: dropRevealLabel is the row header, constant across shapes; the four dropRevealVariants are the value line under it, chosen by which shape actually dropped. dropRevealCappedVariant fires instead of a variant when the pouch is already full; {shape} substitutes the shape noun (straight/elbow/tee/cross piece) same as the variants use. cleanRunBanked/cleanRunCapped replace the two existing CLEAN RUN em strings in place (pouch cap raised 3 to 5, cell to random piece). gridlockChipLabel is a new bullet in the existing kp-chip-breakdown list, lowercase to match its siblings ('3 rotations over par', '1 trap sprung', 'hit the turn cap'), paired with a -6 value; only render it when the win was a gridlock win, a new condition alongside the existing r.capWin check.

copy.desc: Win a dive with zero strain billed and bank one random patch piece. The pouch holds five at most, so a clean win on a full pouch banks nothing.

patchPieces.heading: PATCH PIECES
paragraphs: Slag blocks used to take a flat cell. Now they take a shaped piece: straight, elbow, tee, or cross. Whatever arms a piece rolls on pickup are the arms it keeps, nothing rotates once it is in your pouch.
Craft two pieces at the bench into the union of their arms. Legal only when the result is strictly bigger than both pieces you started with; equal or smaller, the bench will not make the join.
Three ways into the pouch: buy blind off the darknet, pull one from a cleared job, or bank a random piece on a clean win. Five pieces, pouch capped.
patchPieces.suggestedPlacement: after THE KIT section, before AUGMENTS

boostBays.heading: BOOST BAYS
paragraphs: Boosts install into bays, three of them to start. Configs are not boosts and never count against the cap.
A full bay does not block a new boost, it swaps one: take the drop or keep what is already installed. Buy more bays at day close. First one runs 150 cr, the next 300.

copy.text: SEVERED. Its territory walls your port off from the core. No rotation and no patch piece opens a route, so the link is already lost.

items.notes: Noun swap only, rest of the line unchanged as instructed.

items.notes: Kept to the brief's direction; 'arms exactly as held' replaces the old fixed 'cross junction' phrasing now that shape varies and pieces are never rotatable in hand.

items.title: PATCH PIECE
lines: You are carrying a piece. Click a slag block within reach to fuse it in for 1 RAM. One use, then it is gone.
Arms land exactly as held, never rotating once placed. Fit it to the wall you cannot route around, not the first slag you see.

items.title: NIGHT SHOP
lines: You can no longer choose a shape. DARKNET.LNK sells one blind pull, price climbing by the day.
Night patch still buys your strain back. Buy an extra boost bay tonight to raise your cap above 3.

items.title: PATCH CRAFT
lines: Craft two pieces at night or from the loadout bench: free, and you get the union of both pieces' arms.
You only get the craft when the union beats both inputs outright. Equal or smaller spends both pieces for nothing.

items.title: AUGMENT DRAFT
lines: Clearing a ticket offers three augments. Pick one and it holds for the rest of the run.
Three tickets a day, so a clean day banks three picks. CONFIG unlocks a mode, BOOST bends the economy. A full bay swaps instead of blocking.

items.title: BAY FULL
lines: Boost bays are full. Take this pick and you choose one installed boost to bench in its place.
CONFIGS never count against the cap and are never affected by a swap.
